messages:
support: FYI customer ACCT-9982 reports intermittent AccessDenied on KMS Decrypt right after our automated rotation. They also note a short gap in CloudTrail KMS:Decrypt entries. Opening thread to correlate repro steps and next actions.

marta: thanks — how severe? service impact?

support: low-volume ingest failures, retries spiking. Errors started ~2026-03-05T02:12Z right after rotation Lambda ran.

sam: paste one of the error lines from our logs?

support: redacted API log snippet:

```
2026-03-05T02:12:40Z ERROR decrypt 403 KMSAccessDenied: Access denied for Encrypt/Decrypt
requestId=abcd-1234
model=request-infer | customerId=ACCT-9982 | keyId=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/aaaa-bbbb-cccc
```

aria: CloudTrail shows PutAlias/CreateKey at 02:11:58 and PutKeyPolicy at 02:12:01, but Decrypt events for that key are absent between 02:11:00 and 02:15:30.

security-oncall: common culprits: encryption context mismatch, grants not reattached to new key, or caller caching alias->key mapping. Did the customer pass EncryptionContext?

eugene: repro suggestion to share with customer (boto3 example):

```
# simulate decrypt using boto3
python - <<'PY'
import boto3, base64
kms=boto3.client('kms', region_name='us-west-2')
ctxt={'service':'redwood-ingest','account':'ACCT-9982'}
ct = {k: str(v) for k,v in ctxt.items()}
cipher = 'BASE64_CIPHERTEXT_SAMPLE'
try:
    kms.decrypt(CiphertextBlob=base64.b64decode(cipher), EncryptionContext=ct)
    print('ok')
except Exception as e:
    print(repr(e))
PY
```

marta: also check key grants and policy; if rotation created a new CMK and moved the alias, grants attached to the old key won't carry over. Commands we should run:

```
aws kms list-grants --key-id <key-arn>
aws kms get-key-policy --key-id <key-arn> --policy-name default
```

support: customer says they used our rotation Lambda (we ship it). It does CreateKey, CreateAlias, then schedule deletion on old key. They claim old key not deleted yet. Lambda logs show alias swap at 02:11:58.

devops-bot: :gear: rotation-lambda ACCT-9982 ran 2026-03-05T02:11:58Z status=SUCCESS alias=alias/customer/ACCT-9982 -> key/aaaa-bbbb-cccc

aria: requests in our logs referenced the key id that previously mapped to a different CMK, which explains CloudTrail gap if callers kept referencing the old id while alias pointed elsewhere.

security-oncall: EncryptionContext map must match exactly; any type/ordering difference will cause KMS to reject. Also confirm session/STS scope — session policies can remove kms:Decrypt even if key policy allows. CloudTrail shows an AssumeRole at 02:11:55 for service/infer.

sam: on our side, runtime/infer caches alias resolutions in alias_cache.go with a TTL=5m. If rotation happened inside TTL, some pods may still call the cached key id.

eugene: mitigation options: 1) add an explicit grant on the new key for the Redwoo d role so Decrypt succeeds immediately; 2) reattach grants/policy to old key until all callers have switched; 3) invalidate alias cache and restart affected pods.

marta: quick commands for a grant: 

```
aws kms create-grant --key-id <new-key-id> --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/redwood-ingest-role --operations Decrypt
```

support: customer ran the CLI test: Decrypt against new key returns AccessDenied, old key sometimes succeeds until alias swap. They provided an audit snippet showing requests referencing old key id post-swap.

aria: that is consistent with an alias race + cached id. If old key had grants removed or policy changed, those requests would begin failing once alias pointed elsewhere.

security-oncall: we should also look for grant propagation delays and grant tokens; AWS docs warn about eventual propagation.

eugene: evidence collection plan for customer/compliance: export Lambda rotation logs (CloudWatch), CloudTrail events for CreateKey/CreateAlias/PutKeyPolicy/CreateGrant, our API error traces, and customer CloudTrail/CloudWatch snippets for cross-correlation.

marta: assign next actions: support collects customer CLI outputs and non-PII sample ciphertext; eng-runtime implements alias_cache invalidation and schedules rolling restart; security-oncall will create temporary grant and document; infra will update key policy if missing principal after approval.

eng-runtime: can you invalidate alias cache per-customer and do a small rolling restart? minimize blast radius.

eng-runtime: we'll add programmatic invalidation and target a 2-hour patch + controlled rolling restart for ACCT-9982. Creating task ENGR-4021.

devops-bot: :white_check_mark: task created #ENGR-4021 invalidate-alias-cache target=2h

support: customer requested signed attestation for compliance. Can security produce a summary + logs?

security-oncall: yes — we'll prepare an attestation bundle with timestamps, CloudTrail snippets we have, rotation Lambda logs, and our internal error traces. If CloudTrail has missing Decrypt entries for that window we'll explain observed delivery delays and include alternative evidence.

aria: recommended long-term safe rotation sequence to provide zero downtime: 1) pre-create new CMK and attach grants/policies 2) propagate grants and wait for propagation 3) switch alias during low traffic window 4) invalidate caches across runtime fleet 5) monitor for errors for 48h before retiring old key.

support: customer agreed to temporary grant. They will hold deletion of old key and send the requested samples.

security-oncall: note — grant creation is quick but may require grant token handling; see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/grant-api.html

marta: will follow up after eng-runtime rollout and support confirmation. Closing loop when customer confirms decrypts are successful.

support: thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

aws-bot: Reminder: if you create grants, they are subject to propagation delays and grant tokens.
